question: In which of the following languages is ‘Childhood Days - A Memoir’ by Satyajit Ray written?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ‘Childhood Days - A Memoir’** was written in **Bengali **by **Satyajit Ray**.
 
• **"Childhood Days - A Memoir" **is one of Ray's literary works where he delves into his own **childhood experiences**.
 
• In this memoir, Ray offers readers a glimpse into his formative years, growing up in Calcutta (now Kolkata), West Bengal, India.
 
• Through vivid storytelling and introspection, he captures the essence of his childhood, including his family life, education, friendships, and the cultural milieu of early 20th-century Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyajit Ray** is widely recognized as one of the most influential film directors in cinema history. His acclaimed works, including **"The Apu Trilogy," "The Music Room," "The Big City," "Charulata," and the "Goopy-Bagha" trilogy, **highlight his remarkable talent for storytelling and his ability to capture the complexities of human experience on film.
 
• Born in Calcutta to author Sukumar Ray, Ray initially pursued a career as a commercial artist. However, his encounter with French filmmaker Jean Renoir and exposure to groundbreaking films like Vittorio De Sica's **"Bicycle Thieves" **inspired him to delve into independent filmmaking.
 
• In 1992, the Government of India honored Ray with the Bharat Ratna, its highest civilian award, in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the arts.
 
• Additionally, to commemorate Ray's birth centenary, the International Film Festival of India renamed its annual **Lifetime Achievement Award **to the **"Satyajit Ray Lifetime Achievement Award"** in 2021, acknowledging his enduring legacy in the world of cinema.
